reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

answer.evidence: The tile fills the whole 16-row cell with repeating light/mid/dark roof-tile stripe rows. Column x=7 shows light rows at 1, 5, 9 and 13 with mid rows below each. The roof plane runs rows 0-13 and ends in a light front-edge line at row 13, followed by eave shadow at rows 14-15 (mid, then dark). No wall or front face sits below the eave, so only about 2 rows could count as front face, under the 3-row minimum. The right-hand columns (x=11 onward) are a uniform dark strip, which looks like a roof edge or border and not a receding side face. Because the cell has a roof top and no 3-row front face, it reads as a top-down slab. It is a roof fill piece that would depend on neighbouring cells for a wall.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny teal block of horizontal slats, about one tile or less, with no roof, walls, door or windows, so it is not a whole building like the references. It has 5 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references. It shows only about 3 lightness steps, where the references show 5-6 on their roofs, plaster and stone. Its edge pixels are tinted (0% near-neutral), so the outline is a dark teal material tone and not near-black. It has no roof-tile scallops, plaster speckle or stone-by-stone shading. The 0% near-flat figure is a count of small repeated stripes and does not make up for the missing structure. As a stand-in for a building it is much thinner and flatter than either reference.

surfaces.part: tiled roof/wall plane with offset stripe courses and a darker right-hand strip

answer.evidence: The cell is a full-width (15 px) fragment. Rows 0-12 repeat a 4-row tile course pattern (light row, two mid rows, dark row, offset between courses), which reads as a roof or tile plane. Column x=11 stays dark (#126068) over rows 0-12, a flat vertical strip rather than a receding side face. Row 13 is a light edge line (#68c6b2), followed by mid-tone row 14 and dark row 15, which are eave shadow. Only about 2 rows lie below the edge line, so there is no real front face of 3+ rows. The cell is therefore a flat roof/tile surface with just an edge and eave, not a standing volume with a visible south face.

The cell contains no wall, door or lintel. The only face below the edge line is those 2 rows, so there is no real front face. The dark right strip is a shaded edge band, not a drawn side face. This looks like a roof-tile kit piece rather than a complete structure.

surfaces.part: tiled roof-like plane filling the whole cell

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 15-wide rectangle on all 16 rows. The fill is a repeating 4-row tile pattern: a light line (rows 1, 5, 9, 13), then mid-tone rows, then a dark row (rows 4, 8, 12, 15). This reads as shingle or roof-tile courses, or a flat wall texture, so I count it as a roof plane (evidence c). Column x=11 is a dark vertical strip (rows 0-12) at the right edge, which looks like trim rather than a receding side face. The bottom rows 13-15 (light line, mid, dark) are the only eave-like edge. There is no separate vertical front face of 3 or more rows, no lintel, door or wall below the tiles, and no overall gate, pavilion or building silhouette. The cell looks like a seamless kit fragment, not a standalone structure, so it reads as a flat slab with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny teal block of about one tile (roughly 16x30 px at 2x), not a whole building with roof, walls and door/windows, so it does not match the reference kind. It shows a few horizontal teal plank or slat bands with a lighter top edge, so roughly 3 shading steps against 5-6 in the references. There is no real outline: the edge pixels are tinted dark teal (0% neutral), but that is a side effect of the tiny size, not deliberate outlining. It has no tile scallops, no plaster speckle, no stone shading and no grain. The measured 0% near-flat coverage comes from the stripe banding, not from richly varied texture. Nowhere near a house at the Beodeul standard, so it fails.
